It is not possible to tile an 8x8 chessboard with 2x1 dominoes if two opposite corners are removed. Here's why:

A standard 8x8 chessboard has 64 squares, evenly divided into 32 black and 32 white squares. Each 2x1 domino, regardless of its orientation, always covers one black square and one white square. Therefore, for a complete tiling to be possible, the number of black and white squares must be equal.

When two opposite corners are removed, both of these corners are of the same color (either both black or both white). This results in 30 squares of one color and 32 of the other. Since each domino must cover one square of each color, the imbalance in the number of black and white squares makes it impossible to tile the board completely with dominoes.

Thus, the tiling is not possible due to the unequal distribution of square colors after the removal of the two opposite corners.
